front_line: The science may be real. The stock still asks you to pay for the ending before the movie starts
thesis: IonQ may become one of the most important quantum companies in the world, but that is not the same thing as being investable today. The company has real momentum and early commercial traction, but the thesis still depends on technical milestones, long commercialization timelines, and future use cases that are not mature enough to underwrite with confidence.
moat: Differentiated technology in an unresolved architecture race is a bet, not a moat — distribution is rented from rivals and switching costs are near-zero.
risks: Gross margin fell 63% → 40% → 24% — the opposite of a scaling platform, and the single most damning number in the packet.

drafts.x_post: IonQ ($IONQ) builds quantum computers using trapped ions — individual charged atoms held in place and manipulated with lasers to run calculations that classical computers struggle with. Dead Simple Score: 49/100. Status: Pass.

Watchlist.

Watchlist because the payoff is real but the price already assumes the win, and the single most important number — organic revenue mix and gross-margin direction — resolves on the next earnings print. It moves to Open if the Q2 report shows gross margin recovering toward 40%+ with disclosed organic quantum-access usage as the growth driver; it stays off the table if margin sits at or below 24% for another quarter while shares keep climbing.
